title: HoneyBook Pricing 2026: Plans, Fees and Total Cost
summary: HoneyBook pricing includes Starter, Essentials, and Premium tiers. Compare what each plan offers and their costs to select your best option.
body_markdown:
## Connecting HoneyBook to the rest of your tools with Activepieces


A shared platform keeps your client list in one place, but it stops at its own edges.


Activepieces, a workflow tool that moves information between apps and runs unlimited flows on every plan, including the free one, is one way to carry a booked client past them.


It doesn't change what HoneyBook costs you. It changes what happens to a client after they sign.


Here's the cost of doing nothing. HoneyBook's built-in automations work inside HoneyBook:


- they send emails
- they assign tasks
- they move a project through its stages
- they remind clients about invoices


Its integrations cover a set of outside tools, but per its docs, several handoffs a small business needs aren't among them. Someone ends up retyping, and retyping is where a missed invoice or a forgotten welcome message starts.


The gaps below are the ones that show up most often when a client books:


> Someone ends up retyping, and retyping is where a missed invoice or a forgotten welcome message starts.


- Adding a new booked client as a row in a spreadsheet you use for tracking revenue or capacity.
- Creating an entry in your accounting software when a payment comes in, rather than keying it in by hand later.
- Posting an alert to a team chat channel so the person who runs the project knows a client just signed.
- Passing the client's details to a tool HoneyBook has no direct connection to, such as a scheduling app or a mailing list.


Each of these is small. Together they're the unpaid hour at the end of the week that nobody budgeted for.


Activepieces fills them by working as a middle step. You pick a trigger, such as "a new client has booked," and then tell it what to do next: add the spreadsheet row, create the accounting entry, post the chat message.


That flow is one run at 1 credit however many steps it has, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.


You build this by choosing steps on screen, so you don't need to write code.


The apps it can reach number 747 integrations, counted from the MIT-licensed open source monorepo on GitHub, so the spreadsheet, accounting and chat tools above are likely already in that list.


Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and because the core is MIT-licensed, the code behind every one of those connections sits in the repository's packages/integrations/community folder, where the 747 are counted.


If you would rather not send client details through another company's hosting, Activepieces can also be run on your own server, and the free self-hosted Community Edition covers the automation core.


Two cautions, in the spirit of a straight estimate. First, this is a second tool to set up and check, and past the free plan's 1,000 credits a month it has its own bill: Plus is $20 a month for 10,000 credits.


It also only helps if the connection you need exists in Activepieces and HoneyBook exposes the event you want to start from.


Test it with a dummy client before you rely on it. Second, a team of one with a handful of clients a month may do fine copying details by hand.


If you're booking steadily and passing details between three or four apps, the workflow layer pays for itself in hours you stop spending on copying.
